edges.relation: Structured prime-field seeds can be scored and refined in lag space.
Lag residues provide the local fields that warning propagation summarizes.
Field-guided packet moves can be transferred from lag space to sparse Gram-defect repair.
Defect density is a natural local control signal for adaptive schedules.
The symbolic defect state is the training substrate for a learned CA.
Sparse defects can be approximated by syndrome graphs and decoder rules.
Decoder-graph stress and clause stress are two views of the same local inconsistency map.
Clause neighborhoods can be scored by local tensor contraction before exact repair.
A residual screen becomes a stronger local micro-solver when promoted from counting to min-sum optimization.
Learned local rules suggest which compact CA families are expressive enough for generative search.
Seed-generation CA ideas and full generative CA search share the same local-rule design space but differ in how strongly they commit to it.

bridge_chains.rationale: Seed-generation ideas from finite-field CA feed into lag-space diagnostics, then into message-guided and finally defect-guided repair with local self-tuning.
Coding-theory decoders lead to clause-stress transport, then to tensor lookahead, and finally to exact local spin-glass packet optimization.
A learned repair rule can be viewed as an empirical probe for whether compact generative CA rules are expressive enough to emit Hadamard structure directly.
Structured CA seeds, exact near-solution repair, and tensor-assisted local lookahead form a practical seed-to-repair-to-screen pipeline.
